name: Nuls
rootCause: The well-known public chain NULS suffered a hacker attack and lost nearly $480,000 worth of NULS tokens. The SlowMist security team analyzed and found that the reason for the attack was that there was a loophole in the NULS transaction signature verification algorithm. The hacker bypassed the signature verification by using a carefully constructed transaction, transferred the tokens of the team account, and then some tokens were thrown into the market. , At present, major exchanges have suspended the deposit and withdrawal of NULS. After the attack, the official urgently checked the problem, carried out problem repair and code testing, and then release…

descriptions.text: The well-known public chain NULS suffered a hacker attack and lost nearly $480,000 worth of NULS tokens. The SlowMist security team analyzed and found that the reason for the attack was that there was a loophole in the NULS transaction signature verification algorithm. The hacker bypassed the signature verification by using a carefully constructed transaction, transferred the tokens of the team account, and then some tokens were thrown into the market. , At present, major exchanges have suspended the deposit and withdrawal of NULS. After the attack, the official urgently checked the problem, carried out problem repair and code testing, and then release…

On December 23, 2019, the Nuls blockchain was exploited due to a reported signature verification flaw in version 2.2, enabling unauthorized transactions. Approximately 2 million NULS tokens (~$480,000) were stolen, with around 548,354 sold before detection. The network halted further loss by hard forking to destroy unrecoverable tokens. A flaw in the transaction signature verification logic in Nuls version 2.2 allowed attackers to generate valid-looking transactions without legitimate authorization signatures. The technical specifics of the bypass remain undisclosed in public technical documentation.
